item.title: Economic Survey 2026: ‘Development is, in itself, a form of adaptation’
item.description: The Economic Survey 2025-2026 emphasizes integrating adaptation with development plans, highlighting resilient infrastructure, enhanced agricultural productivity, and reliable energy access as key to climate resilience. It stresses domestic financial resources.

item.title: Economic Survey 2026: Centre cites stronger rural economy to replace MGNREGA with VB-GRAMG
item.description: The Economic Survey 2026 suggests replacing MGNREGA with VB-GRAMG due to a stronger rural economy. Despite falling demand for MGNREGA, experts warn that data mismatches and budget caps could exclude genuine beneficiaries, questioning the government's rationale.

item.title: Economic Survey 2026: Raise urea price, provide direct benefit transfers to farmers to curb overuse
item.description: The Economic Survey 2025-26 suggests raising urea prices and providing direct cash transfers to farmers to curb overuse and improve soil health. This aims to correct nutrient imbalances and promote balanced fertilisation, addressing the excessive nitrogen application that has harmed soil quality.

item.title: Tanzania is losing fertile land to soil erosion: What’s happening and what can be done
item.description: Tanzania faces a severe soil erosion crisis, threatening food security and livelihoods. Gully erosion, exacerbated by land-use changes and population pressure, demands urgent restoration efforts. Indigenous practices and community-led solutions offer hope, but large-scale investment is crucial.
